summary: POSIX timer fires one tick late
root_cause: cpukit/score/src/core/timercancel.c:97: the guard used <= where the spec requires <, so a timer due at the current tick was re-queued for the next tick.
fix: Changed <= to < in _Timer_Cancel's expiry comparison; added an assertion in psxtimer01 that a timer expiring at 'now' fires in the same tick.
tests: Reproduced: psxtimer01 timed out waiting for the callback (1 tick late) before the fix: 'expected tick 5, fired at tick 6'.
After the fix: psxtimer01 passes; psxtimes and psxtimersuites on sparc/erc32 SIS: 412/412 passed.
Full psx subset on erc32-sis: 1284 passed, 0 failed.
reproduction: psxtimer01 hung for one extra tick before the fix
risk: Any timer expiring in the current tick is now delivered immediately; this is the POSIX-required behaviour. Periodic (rtems_timer) timers are unaffected: they re-arm before the comparison.
lesson: RTEMS timer paths compare ticks as '< due' vs 'now'; off-by-one shows as a one-tick-late callback in psxtimer tests.
